source.title: Schema-learning and rebinding as mechanisms of in-context learning and emergence
source.authors: Siva K. Swaminathan; A. Dedieu; Rajkumar Vasudeva Raju; M. Shanahan; Miguel Lázaro-Gredilla; Dileep George

record.file_problem: none; full paper text is present
record.tranche_reason: The paper discusses induction heads as a prior explanation of ICL, but its experiments use clone-structured causal graphs (CSCGs), not transformers, and do not measure induction heads or the specific behaviors in the claim versions.
record.gate_note: The paper cites prior work on induction heads but reports no new induction-head results. Its own results measure ICL accuracy in CSCGs, which is related to the claim’s subject but does not test the listed induction-head versions. The rows below record selected reported ICL-accuracy conditions; other GINC context/example combinations and per-task LIALT results are not included.
record.test_reason: All experiments use clone-structured causal graphs (CSCGs), not transformers. No attention heads, previous-token composition, training trajectories or token-index loss are measured. Induction heads appear only as cited prior work (ref [5]). The transformer-mechanism section (Sec. 6, Fig. 8) is a conjecture with no transformer results. The CSCG ICL-accuracy results bear on in-context learning in a different model class, not on any induction-head version.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors show that CSCGs acquire ICL through three mechanisms: learning template (schema) circuits, retrieving them by context, and rebinding novel tokens to template slots. Capacity affects which abilities emerge. They conjecture, without testing, that transformer layers implement similar mixed content and position templates selected via attention. Induction heads are only cited.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use CSCGs and measure prompt-completion accuracy; they do not reproduce or directly test the original induction-head method.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports that CSCG ICL accuracy changes with model capacity/overallocation ratio and with GINC context length; it also reports failure on GINC prompts from concepts unseen during training.

fits_no_version.finding: On GINC, a 50-clone CSCG reaches about 0.97 ICL accuracy at k=8 and 10. A 10-clone CSCG reaches about 0.68–0.70.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In non-transformer sequence models (CSCGs), ICL accuracy on GINC depends on latent capacity.

fits_no_version.finding: On LIALT, average ICL accuracy rises from 0.00 to about 0.9 as the overallocation ratio goes from 0.1 to 3.0, for both instruction-based and example-based prompts.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: ICL of algorithms with novel tokens can arise in CSCGs via schema retrieval and rebinding, with accuracy depending on overparameterization.

record.problems: The empirical models are CSCGs rather than transformers, and the study does not identify or intervene on induction heads. Its transformer-mechanism discussion is conjectural. The reported ICL measures are task accuracy, not token-index loss or induction-head formation timing.
record.rows_left_out: Other GINC context-length/example-count combinations in Appendix C, Table 1 and the per-task LIALT accuracy tables in Appendix D.3 are not itemized; they concern CSCG ICL accuracy and do not test any listed induction-head version. Also omitted are LIALT results after EM convergence, which the authors describe as mostly identical to the single-iteration results.

untested.parts: No transformers and no previous-token or induction heads are studied. The [A][B]…[A]→[B] mechanism is not examined.
No training-time trajectory of heads, no loss-curve bump, and no phase-change timing are measured. Capacity is varied, but training time is not tracked.
No large transformers are studied. The contribution of induction heads to ICL is not measured. The ICL measure is task accuracy, not loss falling with token index.
No search for induction behaviour across model families, sizes or runs. The CSCG is a different architecture and no induction heads are identified in it.
The dependence of induction-head formation on data or training setup is not tested. CSCG capacity dependence concerns ICL accuracy only.
Proposes schema retrieval and rebinding as an alternative ICL account, but never compares it against induction heads in any transformer.
No stages of induction-head formation are measured.

record.verdict_notes: The rows are correctly linked to 'none'. Their cannot_determine states are reasonable because none of the measures bears on an induction-head version. The paper is a NeurIPS 2023 publication. The dax-test results (Fig. 7) are qualitative and also bear on no version.

versions.untested_parts: No transformer heads or previous-token-head composition are studied; the [A][B] … [A] → [B] mechanism is not tested.
No induction-head training trajectory, token-index loss, or loss-curve bump is measured.
No large transformers or induction-head contribution to their ICL are measured; the paper reports CSCG ICL accuracy, not loss falling with token index.
No induction behavior across transformer model families, sizes, or training runs is measured.
The study varies CSCG capacity and evaluates dataset conditions, but does not test whether induction heads form or how their formation depends on data or training setup.
The study does not compare induction heads with other mechanisms as carriers of few-shot learning in transformers.
No stages or sub-steps in induction-head formation are measured.
